bugs.title: Crisis keyword detection fails when user types in all caps
bugs.description: When a user types a crisis-related phrase in all capital letters (e.g., 'I WANT TO HURT MYSELF'), the crisis detection algorithm does not trigger the escalation flow. The system continues with normal conversation instead of routing to the crisis protocol. Reported by customer service after a user complained they did not receive crisis resources when expressing distress.
bugs.notes: Safety critical. Crisis detection is a core safety feature. Failure to detect could result in a user in crisis not receiving appropriate resources.

bugs.title: Typo in gratitude journaling prompt on day 3
bugs.description: The gratitude journaling prompt on day 3 reads 'What are you gratful for today?' instead of 'What are you grateful for today?'. Noticed during internal review.
bugs.notes: Typo does not impact intended function of the product. Does not fail a user need or product requirement.

bugs.title: Mood check-in score not saved when user backgrounds app mid-entry
bugs.description: If a user starts the daily mood check-in, selects their mood score, but then backgrounds the app before hitting submit, when they return the mood score is lost and they have to start over. Three user reports in the past two weeks.
bugs.notes: Annoying but not clinically significant. User can redo the check-in. Deviation from intended function since data should persist.

bugs.title: Sentiment analysis misclassifies sarcasm as positive affect
bugs.description: Multiple instances where users expressing sarcastic statements like 'Oh yeah I'm doing just great' are being classified as positive mood by the sentiment model. The chatbot then responds with reinforcement of the 'positive' mood rather than probing further. Identified through clinical review of conversation logs.
bugs.notes: Clinically significant. Misreading negative affect as positive could reinforce avoidance and undermine therapeutic alliance. Systematic issue across the sentiment model.

bugs.title: Push notification displays raw HTML tags
bugs.description: Some push notification reminders are showing raw HTML like 'Time for your check-in!' instead of rendered bold text. Appears to affect Android devices running OS 14+.
bugs.notes: Cosmetic but affects user experience. The notification still arrives and is readable, but looks unprofessional and could reduce user trust.

bugs.title: Therapist handoff email contains wrong patient session summary
bugs.description: A therapist reported receiving a handoff email where the session summary attached belonged to a different patient. This has been confirmed in one instance. Investigation shows a race condition in the API when two handoff requests are processed within the same second.
bugs.notes: Critical patient safety and privacy issue. PHI was sent to the wrong provider. Even though probability is low, severity is maximum. HIPAA implications.

bugs.title: Progress dashboard graph Y-axis label overlaps with data points
bugs.description: On the progress dashboard, when mood scores are consistently in the 1-2 range, the Y-axis label overlaps with the data points making it hard to read exact values. Only occurs on smaller phone screens.
bugs.notes: Minor visual issue. Data is still visible and the dashboard functions as intended. Does not prevent the user from viewing their progress.

bugs.title: CBT thought record does not save alternative thought if over 500 characters
bugs.description: When a user types an alternative thought longer than 500 characters in the CBT thought challenging module, the text is silently truncated without warning. The user sees their full text during entry but only the first 500 characters are saved. Two user complaints received.
bugs.notes: Therapeutically relevant since the user's full thought is part of the CBT exercise. Silent truncation means the user doesn't know their work was lost. Deviation from intended function.

bugs.title: Sleep hygiene program shows Day 4 content on Day 3
bugs.description: Users enrolled in the sleep hygiene program are receiving Day 4 content when they should be seeing Day 3. The issue is traced to a misconfigured content node in the CMS decision tree. Affects all users currently on Day 3 of the program.
bugs.notes: Every user hitting Day 3 gets wrong content. While not dangerous, it disrupts the therapeutic sequence which is designed to build progressively. Clear deviation from product requirements.

bugs.title: App crashes on launch for users who haven't opened app in 90+ days
bugs.description: Users who haven't opened the app in over 90 days experience a crash on launch. The app attempts to sync a large backlog of data and hits a memory limit. Requires the user to delete and reinstall the app, losing local data. Six reports in the past month.
bugs.notes: Users lose their historical data and have to reinstall. For a mental health app, losing your mood tracking history and journal entries is significant. Prevents use of the device entirely until reinstall.

bugs.title: Deprecated onboarding flow accessible via deep link
bugs.description: An old onboarding flow that was deprecated in v2.2 can still be accessed if a user clicks a deep link from an old marketing email. The flow shows outdated content and some broken screens.
bugs.notes: Deprecated feature. Does not meet defect criteria since it is not part of the current released product. Should still be fixed but is not a regulatory concern.

bugs.title: Chatbot conversation loop when user responds with only emojis
bugs.description: When a user responds to the chatbot with only emoji characters (no text), the bot enters a loop where it repeats its last prompt indefinitely. The user has to force close and reopen the app to break the loop. Reported by three users.
bugs.notes: Disrupts the therapeutic session and requires app restart. The intended function is to gracefully handle unexpected inputs and guide the user back to the conversation.

bugs.title: Crisis escalation sends user to outdated hotline number
bugs.description: The crisis escalation flow displays a mental health hotline number that was decommissioned 6 months ago. Users who call it get a 'number not in service' message. Discovered during routine content audit.
bugs.notes: Safety critical. A user in crisis being directed to a dead phone number could delay or prevent them from getting help. Must be corrected immediately.

bugs.title: Android back button skips confirmation on journal entry
bugs.description: On Android, if a user is writing a journal entry and presses the hardware back button, the entry is discarded without a confirmation dialog. iOS correctly shows a 'Save draft?' prompt.
bugs.notes: Inconsistent behavior between platforms. Loss of journal content is frustrating but not clinically harmful. Deviation from intended function since the confirmation dialog is a product requirement.

bugs.title: Font size setting doesn't persist after app update
bugs.description: Users who had set a larger font size for accessibility find that the setting resets to default after updating the app. They have to go back into settings and change it again.
bugs.notes: Accessibility related preference, but font size persistence across updates is not a stated product requirement. It is a usability issue worth fixing but does not meet defect criteria as currently defined.

bugs.title: Thought challenging module skips cognitive distortion identification step
bugs.description: In the CBT thought challenging flow, the step where the user identifies which cognitive distortion applies to their automatic thought is being skipped entirely. The flow jumps straight from 'identify automatic thought' to 'generate alternative thought'. This means users miss a core therapeutic component. Affects all users of the thought challenging module since v2.4.0.
bugs.notes: Clinically significant. The cognitive distortion identification step is a core component of CBT methodology. Skipping it undermines the therapeutic value of the entire module. Affects 100% of users on this flow. Introduced in most recent release.

bugs.title: Loading spinner displays for 8+ seconds on progress dashboard
bugs.description: The progress dashboard takes over 8 seconds to load for users with more than 60 days of mood data. The spinner shows but there is no indication of progress or that data is loading. Two users reported thinking the app was frozen.
bugs.notes: Performance issue that degrades user experience but doesn't prevent function. Dashboard eventually loads. Deviation from intended function since requirement states dashboard should load within 3 seconds.

bugs.title: Unreleased meditation feature visible in navigation menu
bugs.description: A meditation feature currently in development is showing up in the navigation menu for about 5% of users due to a feature flag misconfiguration. Tapping it leads to a blank screen. The feature is not part of any released product version.
bugs.notes: Feature is not part of the released product. Does not meet defect criteria. Still needs to be fixed from a user experience standpoint but is not a complaint or regulatory concern.

bugs.title: Mood check-in allows duplicate submissions within same day
bugs.description: Users can submit the daily mood check-in multiple times in the same day. The progress dashboard then shows multiple data points for that day, which skews the trend visualization. The product requirement states one check-in per day.
bugs.notes: Deviation from product requirement. Not clinically harmful but could affect data integrity for clinical outcomes tracking. Low risk overall.

bugs.title: App icon badge count shows incorrect number of unread notifications
bugs.description: The app icon badge on the home screen sometimes shows 3 unread notifications when there is only 1, or shows 0 when there is 1 pending. Seems to be a caching issue.
bugs.notes: Badge count accuracy is not a stated product requirement. The notifications themselves work correctly. Minor cosmetic issue that doesn't affect product function.
